name: Cafesjian Center for the Arts
funding: Run by the Cafesjian Museum Foundation, which Gerard Cafesjian endowed with over $35M from his West Publishing fortune. Exhibits draw on the Cafesjian Art Trust.
watch: Cafesjian died in 2013. His 2007 to 2011 lawsuit with the Armenian Assembly ended with the court finding he acted in good faith.
records_note: The Cafesjian pages name Gerard Cafesjian as principal benefactor but publish no reports, accounts, sponsor list or board.

name: Cample Line
funding: £127k income (2025). Creative Scotland multi-year funding from April 2025, Holywood Trust, Henry Moore Foundation, Dumfries and Galloway Council, Regional Cultural Fund.
watch: Rural art space near Dumfries. Its website lists no funders; the signed 2025 accounts name them.
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts are on the OSCR register, funders show as unlabelled logos, and the Who We Are page lists the board.

name: CAN Centre d'art Neuchâtel
funding: City of Neuchâtel, Canton of Neuchâtel, Loterie Romande, Pro Helvetia; artist-run non-profit association.

name: Capacete
funding: Arts Collaboratory, international residency fellowships, independent patron circle; non-profit foundation.
watch: Independent residency program founded in 1998 in Santa Teresa / Glória; it makes no commercial sales.

name: CAPC Musée d Art Contemporain
funding: €3.8M. Ville de Bordeaux, DRAC Nouvelle-Aquitaine, les Amis du CAPC.

name: Casa Tres Patios (C3P)
funding: Arts Collaboratory, Prince Claus Fund, Alcaldía de Medellín cultural projects; non-profit foundation.
watch: Non-profit contemporary art centre in Prado Centro; dedicated to critical pedagogy, urban rights, and artistic research since 2006.

name: Casino Luxembourg – Forum d'art contemporain
funding: Financially supported by the Ministère de la Culture, in partnership with Les Amis des Musées d'Art et d'Histoire Luxembourg.
watch: Public kunsthalle dedicated to living artists, with production residencies and research.
records_note: Casino Luxembourg names its nine-member board and shows logos of its ministry funder and its friends' association, but posts no reports or accounts.

name: Castello di Rivoli
funding: 2023 income €5.6M: public grants €3.2M (Regione Piemonte, Turin, Rivoli), private grants €1.3M (Fondazione CRT, CRC, Compagnia di San Paolo); Intesa Sanpaolo and Lavazza Group are partners.
watch: Francesca Lavazza chairs the board. Fondazione Magnetto funds a restoration. No flagged funder, protest or censorship found.
records_note: Rivoli posts yearly accounts and activity reports for 2017 to 2025 with auditors' reports, names its board, and names funders and sponsors in the accounts.

name: Castlefield Gallery
funding: £671k income (FY2025). Arts Council England (to 2027/28), Manchester City Council, Haworth Trust, Brian Mercer Trust, Fenton Arts Trust, corporate and individual donors.
watch: Artist-led registered charity and gallery founded in 1984 on Hewitt Street; supports northern UK artists and affordable studios.
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts are on the Charity Commission register, the support page names patrons and donors undated, and trustees are listed.

name: Catalyst Arts
funding: Arts Council of Northern Ireland, Belfast City Council, member support; artist-run collective.

name: CCA Derry~Londonderry
funding: Arts Council of Northern Ireland is the primary funder; Derry City and Strabane District Council, Garfield Weston Foundation and Caldwell & Robinson Solicitors are also named.
watch: Garfield Weston Foundation is graded as an ordinary trust elsewhere on the map. No controversy, protest or censorship found.
records_note: The NI register holds annual reports 2023 to 2024 and accounts to 2025; the about page names funders undated; no board list on the site.

name: CCA Glasgow (Centre for Contemporary Arts)
funding: Creative Scotland Regular Funding, Glasgow City Council; registered educational charity.
